decision: RETAINED as an equal-output, faster working parent: official score is bit-for-bit the parent's 18428 and the official time is 288s against the parent's 292s, i.e. the same score 4s faster. This meets the clause the L-TF1 card pre-registered in section 3 -- 'an equal official score with a faster official time promotes this candidate to a working parent'. It is NOT the complete root: the current root v231 scores 18518/291s, 90 points higher, so the root is unchanged. v233 instead replaces v230 as the fallback root, which it strictly dominates (same score, 4s faster).
projection_note: no projection was recorded, and none was warranted: the mechanism removes exactly two matrix products per dynamic call, measured locally at 0.386 ms on 128 rows and 2.032 ms on 512 rows against calls costing 534 ms and 874 ms (0.072% and 0.233%), and no clock on this machine could resolve the difference -- the three-arm paired estimator with a byte-identical sham arm reported +3.0 / +7.6 / -8.4 / -9.3 ms while the sham's own median drifted up to +6.9 ms, and the in-process and six-shard readings disagreed in sign. The official machine nonetheless measured a clean -4s. The honest reading is that local wall-clock resolution was the limit, not the mechanism: 'unresolvable locally' did not mean 'zero'.
note: The official baseline for this reading is the v230 root at 18428 / 292s. v233 is a descendant of that root, carrying neither the v231 K=2 arm nor the v232 L-QF1 quadratic correction, so this reading prices the two removed products at K=1 and is not additive with any v231 or v232 result. Every output field is bit-identical to the parent (336/336 paired cases exactly zero), which is why the score is unchanged to the point.
candidate_type: complete Linear L-TF1 candidate (v230 root plus one guarded loop head); the only v233 under solutions/ at archive time; retained as fallback root
